what: VSA against a dense control on the same checkpoint, at two sequence lengths, to see whether the sparse advantage appears where it is supposed to
stack: DRAFT throughout: core PR 15958 (head 10febb01) in the working tree, Kijai/MiniMax-H3-experimental checkpoint, comfy_kitchen 0.2.31+sol.dae00a1. Only the kernel is released.

124_frames.verdict: NOT MEASURED. One run per arm, 1.5 s apart -- that cannot separate 6% from excursion in either direction.

362_frames.verdict: ATTRIBUTABLE. The between-arm gap is about 32 s and the largest within-arm spread is 2.72 s, an order of magnitude smaller. Two samples per arm, not one.

finding: The advantage is length-dependent and appears where sparse attention predicts it should. At 22k rows the difference is inside excursion; at 63k rows VSA is about 1.46x faster than sage on the same checkpoint. TWO POINTS, so this is a direction and not a curve.
correctness_alongside: At both lengths VSA differs from its dense control and each arm reproduces itself at the same seed, verified on decoded pixels with the arms identified from the graph embedded in each file (bench/verify_vsa_render.py).
not_established: ANY quality claim. Speed says nothing about output, a rendered pair cannot A/B a numerical change, and these arms differ in attention regime outright.
that this transfers to the shipped canvas. 63,233 rows is still below every shipped t2v graph, which prices at 109,457.
a comparison against Sol-Attn. The control here is sage, not Sol, so this says nothing about VSA against the sparse attention this repo actually ships.
that keep_percent 10.0 is right; it is the distillation's published sparsity, unmeasured here.

capture_is_narrow_and_cannot_be_re_asked.rule: CLAUDE.md cf459e3, owner 2026-08-30: capture broadly first, decide what it means second. A run recording one number per arm cannot be re-asked a question.
capture_is_narrow_and_cannot_be_re_asked.what_this_run_recorded: total wall time per arm, and a sha256 of the decoded RGB stream. That is two numbers.
questions_it_therefore_cannot_answer: where the time goes -- no per-step or per-stage timing, so the 1.46x cannot be split between attention and everything else, and attention is the only part VSA touches.
whether the difference from dense is concentrated anywhere -- no latents kept, so no fidelity metric can be computed offline at all.
what VRAM did, which is one of the two things a sparse kernel is for.
whether error sits at segment boundaries, which is the open question a peer raised about sage's per-block quantisation and which the same capture would have served.
what_a_re_askable_capture_would_record: the output latent, not the encoded mp4 -- every fidelity question is then an offline scoring pass rather than a re-render.
per-step wall time and peak VRAM.
attention outputs at a few depths, which is what h3_capture.py and the grade_*_on_capture.py family already exist for.
PackedLayout.segments, which is NOT currently in any capture and is what blocks the segment-boundary question for sage as well as VSA. One field, two lanes.
capture_is_narrow_and_cannot_be_re_asked.not_withdrawn: the 1.46x stands as a wall-time observation with two samples per arm and a gap an order of magnitude over the spread. What is recorded here is that it is the ONLY question these two renders can answer.
